kakekotoba.reading_secondary: none - single reading, but note wordplay potential with 休らふ
kakekotoba.interaction: Not a true kakekotoba; 休らはで simply means 'without resting/hesitating (to sleep)'. No second grammatically active meaning found.

bipartite.kami_theme: The speaker regrets not simply going to sleep without hesitation, as night deepened (Sayo fukete)
bipartite.shimo_theme: Instead she stayed awake watching the moon until it sank low in the sky, having waited in vain for a promised visitor
bipartite.pivot_note: The kami-no-ku states a counterfactual wish (I should have just gone to sleep) while the shimo-no-ku reveals the actual, contrasting reality (I watched the moon decline, having waited all night in vain for a lover who never came). The pivot is between what should have happened and what did happen — the poem's core irony is the wasted vigil, only fully understood once the shimo reveals the extent of the wait (until the moon itself tilted toward setting).

kigo.note: The moon (月) alone, without a modifying season word, is the classical autumn moon (aki no tsuki) of waka convention — the quintessential object of nocturnal contemplation and longing in the autumn night sky, prized for its clarity and associated with romantic vigil and yearning.
